channel.title: InvestPR Media Monitoring
channel.description: Coverage this period is dominated by Puerto Rico's severe drought and water-rationing crisis affecting over 180,000 customers, drawing FEMA and National Guard support and renewed scrutiny of aging water infrastructure. On the investment side, the hotel and branded-residential pipeline is reported nearing $4 billion with new international brands entering the market, Genera PR is seeking approval for a $95-165 million FEMA-funded water facility to protect San Juan-area power plants, and DDEC doubled its water-crisis incentive for small businesses to $10,000. Real risks stand out: the Fiscal Oversight Board is questioning PREPA's $5.8 billion emergency generation contract after the vendor said its signature was used without authorization, and separately warned that elevated municipal excise taxes in 22 towns could jeopardize federal reconstruction funding.
